translation: Homage to the all-knowing one.
The knower of this ninefold group, the ordainer — he is called the guru.
Initiation, the impeller(?), the powers — eight; the fives, three — (these are) the modes of conduct.
Dharma and indeed non-carelessness — power is declared fivefold.
The falling away and the destruction of the bound state (paśutva) — the purification is declared fivefold.

sanskrit: dravyaṃ kālaḥ kriyā mūrttiḥ guruścaiveha pañcamaḥ || 5 ||
translation: Substance, time, rite, image, and the guru as the fifth here.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ tapo'tha nityatvaṃ sthitiḥ siddhiśca pañcamī || 6 ||
translation: Knowledge, austerity, and then permanence, stability, and attainment as the fifth.
And indeed grace — the means of the attainments are determined as five.
These five, rooted in the bound state (paśutva), hold the rank of what is to be abandoned in the teaching.
Homage to the seer of all things — for (his) eternity, infinity, and lordship.
Homage to him, the true guru, whose hand is knowledge of the five principles.
The knower of this ninefold group, the ordainer — he is called the guru.
The knower of this ninefold group, the ordainer — he is called the guru.

sanskrit: vā lābhādijñānavikalaḥ sa khalvācāryābhāsa eva nāpavargaganteti || 1 ||
translation: Or he who is devoid of the knowledge of the attainments and so on — he is indeed but a semblance of a teacher; he is not one who goes to liberation, so it is said.
Initiation, the impeller(?), the powers — eight; the fives, three — (these are) the modes of conduct.
Their purification is with water, and the scrubbing with cow-hair.
For them, purity with water is declared — as of the camasa-cups at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatra bhuktvā ca pītvā ca yatiścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret || iti yamaḥ ||
translation: There, having eaten and having drunk, the ascetic should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa — thus the yama.
From the very absence of the body, the mode of conduct is impossible — thus.
Dharma and indeed non-carelessness — power is declared fivefold.
The falling away and the destruction of the bound state (paśutva) — the purification is declared fivefold.

sanskrit: dravyaṃ kālaḥ kriyā mūrtirguruścaiveha pañcamah || 5 || iti
translation: Substance, time, rite, image, and the guru as the fifth here — thus.

sanskrit: puṣpāṇi ca punardhūpaṃ mantrā eṣa kramaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
translation: Flowers, and again incense, and mantras — this is declared the sequence (krama).

sanskrit: sa bhavati mataḥ kila satāmācāryo jñānahetuśca ||
translation: He is regarded, indeed, as a teacher of the good and a cause of knowledge.
He gathers the meanings of the scriptures, and for that the teacher is praised.
But this human circle of transmigration is a single segment (parvan).

sanskrit: yatra vāco nivarttante vāgviśuddhaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ ||
translation: He is declared pure in speech, where words turn back.
Having burnt all his works, he would attain union with Śiva.
The field of Śiva extends a hundred cubits and more from the liṅga on every side.
By withdrawal, the sense-objects; by meditation, the guṇas that are not the Lord.
All defects perish, and he is born abiding in sattva.
A hundred years and more is equal to that single breath-control.
There is nothing higher than that, than breath-control — thus the śruti.
Having bathed for the sake of purification, he should practise the six breath-exercises.
Those whose wealth is austerity drive all that away quickly by austerity alone.
By austerity alone, well performed, they are released from sin.

sanskrit: te nirmalāstattvavido viśuddhā gacchanti mokṣaṃ hyubhayorabhāvāt ||
translation: Stainless, knowers of reality, purified, they go to liberation — because of the absence of both.

sanskrit: puṇyapāpaphale dagdhe svāmī tasya na vidyate || iti |
translation: When the fruit of merit and demerit is burnt, no owner of it remains.
Because of the absence of capacity for the practice of yoga in one who is deficient in the rules and practice of the exposition.

sanskrit: nāsti dharmādṛte yoga iti yogavido viduḥ iti ||
translation: 'There is no yoga without dharma' — thus the knowers of yoga know.
Attainment is higher than non-carelessness; from carelessness, hell is certain.

sanskrit: gururjanaguhādeśaḥ smaśānaṃ rudra eva ca || iti
translation: The guru is the secret instruction; the cremation ground is Rudra himself — thus.
And indeed grace — the means of the attainments are determined as five.
He who investigates by reasoning knows dharma, not another.
At the beginning of the night, at midnight, and at the end of the night — the man of unwavering vow.
Having abandoned attachment to other things, seeing this existence as made of suffering...
Making excessive exertion, increasing the excellence of purity...
Or even for one year he should remain with his mind fixed on that, absorbed in that.
He indeed sees the whole reality, endowed with all its limiting adjuncts.
That which is not seen even by other lords of yoga, other than the Pāśupata.
He who, even without knowing the rule, is of good vow — in these times...
To him even the pleased Lord would give that unsurpassed attainment.
If, meditating on him, the Lord, he releases his vital breaths...
Water-eaters and air-eaters, and those whose conduct is of extremely fierce austerity —
The attainment which they obtain in a thousand years...
Having known thus the greatness of yoga, the certain continuance of the body and so on...
The body is sustained as long as the intellect does not decline.
Likewise he should meditate diligently on Śiva, unmingled with speech and the rest.

sanskrit: tadvattaṃ praṇidhānena divā rātrau ca cintayet ||
translation: Likewise he should contemplate him with focused devotion, by day and by night.
Afterwards he should meditate on him alone with his intellect, having set (everything) apart.
'Thus it is seen by the accomplished ones' — this is the meaning.
In the teaching these five have the bound state (paśutva) as their root, by reason of their status as to-be-abandoned.
By the grace of the teachers (arises) knowledge, characterized by the five principles.
Having known this very supreme (knowledge), he should become one who delights in the practice of yoga.
This knowledge should be given to him — not to another — by one desiring attainment.
By divulging the secret he would go down to the downward course together with his disciples.
By whom the ocean of the five principles was shown with eight good verses.
In the Gaṇakārikā composed by Ācārya Bhāsarvajña, the Ratnaṭīkā is completed.
He who, having taken on a body, stands here for the welfare of Brahmins...
What was said by the author of the Bhāṣya, I will state — the section on the yamas likewise.
Non-stealing, service to the guru, purity, and moderation in food —
Ten indeed, until the body falls, are the yamas of yogins in the five-principle (teaching).
The wise know that as non-violence: the non-arising of suffering for all.
Especially with regard to the senses, celibacy is declared — thus.
For the prohibition of it is declared truth by the investigators of truth.
These seekers of liberation declare: the abandonment of that is non-dealing.
Taking, acquisition by improper means, receiving without entitlement —
The thinkers of this declare: avoidance of that is non-stealing.
Service to the guru is the purification of body, inner organ, and self.
The traditional practice of observance joined with the prescribed rule —
Non-anger and purity of mind, even when one has been harmed by others —
Exertion in practice — that is called non-carelessness.
There, from the sūtra on prepared food, non-violence is declared to be obtained.
Likewise celibacy and truth, from the instruction of the exposition and the like.
From the sūtra: non-dwelling; non-stealing, from the unrelaxed prohibition.
From the ash-bath of the body, and likewise by the touchings and so on —
And likewise lightness of food — (eating) alms-food as it is obtained, abandoned (by others).
From the instruction on muttering and non-carelessness, non-carelessness is declared a yama.
Having drawn (it) out from the essential meaning alone, the section on the yamas has been made.
Lokākṣi and Jaigīṣavya, and likewise Dadhivāhana —

sanskrit: śvetaḥ śūlyatha daṇḍī ca sahiṣṇuḥ somaśarmakaḥ || 3 ||
translation: Śveta, and then Śūlin(?), Daṇḍin, and Sahiṣṇu, Somaśarman —
For the liberation of the twice-born, from the boon-granting of Rudra, and likewise of Bhṛgu —
Having bowed to Lakulin, and to him, I speak this something.
I go to the liberation declared by the Pañcārtha scripture; do likewise.
By that (nature of yours as) the grace-giver to devotees, have compassion on me, your devotee.

sanskrit: na gamyate yathā mārgo viruddhaḥ kriyatāṃ tathā || 8 ||
translation: As the path is not traversed (when) obstructed, so let it be made.

sanskrit: vairāgyaṃ me dhruvaṃ dehi śarīrārogyatāṃ tathā || 9 ||
translation: Give me firm dispassion, and likewise health of body.
O Lord, let it be practised thus; may my Pañcilā be accomplished.
Let equal regard toward all beings be established in me.
